/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown
  Typed reasons for an unknown verdict, and the three-valued result that carries them.

  A monitor that says `unknown` without saying why is useless for diagnosis. Every place that
  produces `u` attaches a reason; the connectives keep the reasons of their unknown operands and
  drop them once a value is decided.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Tri
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Units
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Handles

namespace TrafficSpec

inductive UnknownReason
  | absentAtom (name : String)            -- the source did not observe this atom for this entity
  | samplingGap (op : String)             -- observations too sparse for the window
  | windowTruncated (op : String)         -- the window reaches past the start or end of the trace
  | identityGap (track : TrackId)         -- a bound track is not present and no link continues it
  | assumptionMissing (id : AsmId)        -- an `asm.*` the scene did not supply
  | intentionMissing (id : IntId)         -- an `int.*` the scene did not declare for the road user at the region
  | parameterMissing (name : String)      -- a reading parameter the rule names but the reading lacks
  | unboundVariable (name : String)       -- a formula variable with no binding
  | compositionUnknown (rule : String)    -- a composed rule reported unknown or does not exist
  | outOfRange                            -- an index outside the trace
  | divisionByZero (what : String)
  | malformed (what : String)             -- a literal that names no enumeration value, wrong arity
  | undefined (concept : String)          -- the concept's precondition does not hold here (e.g. a multi-lane configuration)
  | aggregateUnresolved (id : String)     -- the posted definition of the aggregate decides neither inclusion nor exclusion of the road user's class
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

namespace UnknownReason
/-- A stable spelling for reports and histograms. -/
def tag : UnknownReason → String
  | .absentAtom n => s!"absent_atom:{n}"
  | .samplingGap op => s!"sampling_gap:{op}"
  | .windowTruncated op => s!"window_truncated:{op}"
  | .identityGap t => s!"identity_gap:{t}"
  | .assumptionMissing id => s!"assumption_missing:{id}"
  | .intentionMissing id => s!"intention_missing:{id}"
  | .parameterMissing n => s!"parameter_missing:{n}"
  | .unboundVariable n => s!"unbound_variable:{n}"
  | .compositionUnknown r => s!"composition_unknown:{r}"
  | .outOfRange => "out_of_range"
  | .divisionByZero w => s!"division_by_zero:{w}"
  | .malformed w => s!"malformed:{w}"
  | .undefined c => s!"undefined:{c}"
  | .aggregateUnresolved id => s!"aggregate_unresolved:{id}"
instance : ToString UnknownReason := ⟨tag⟩
end UnknownReason

/-- A three-valued result with the reasons behind an unknown one. -/
structure R where
  v : Tri
  why : List UnknownReason := []
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace R
def t : R := ⟨.t, []⟩
def f : R := ⟨.f, []⟩
def u (w : UnknownReason) : R := ⟨.u, [w]⟩
def ofBool (b : Bool) : R := ⟨Tri.ofBool b, []⟩
def ofOption (o : Option Bool) (w : UnknownReason) : R :=
  match o with
  | some b => ofBool b
  | none => u w
/-- Reasons are kept only while the value is undecided. -/
def settle (v : Tri) (why : List UnknownReason) : R := ⟨v, if v = .u then why.eraseDups else []⟩
@[simp] theorem settle_v (v : Tri) (why : List UnknownReason) : (settle v why).v = v := rfl
def and (a b : R) : R := settle (Tri.and a.v b.v) (a.why ++ b.why)
def or (a b : R) : R := settle (Tri.or a.v b.v) (a.why ++ b.why)
def not (a : R) : R := ⟨Tri.not a.v, a.why⟩
@[simp] theorem and_v (a b : R) : (and a b).v = Tri.and a.v b.v := rfl
@[simp] theorem or_v (a b : R) : (or a b).v = Tri.or a.v b.v := rfl
@[simp] theorem not_v (a : R) : (not a).v = Tri.not a.v := rfl
def implies (a b : R) : R := or (not a) b
def all (xs : List R) : R := xs.foldl and t
def any (xs : List R) : R := xs.foldl or f
/-- Lift an `Option α` into a computation that is unknown when the option is empty. -/
def bindOpt {α : Type} (o : Option α) (w : UnknownReason) (k : α → R) : R :=
  match o with
  | some a => k a
  | none => u w
end R

/-- A quantity that may be unknown, with the reason. -/
abbrev QR := Except UnknownReason Q

/-- Kleene conjunction and disjunction over index ranges of a per-instant array in O(1) each,
    from prefix counts and next-unknown pointers. Reasons come from the earliest unknown in range. -/
structure RangeAgg where
  vals : Array R
  prefF : Array Nat      -- prefF[i] = number of false values before index i
  prefT : Array Nat
  prefU : Array Nat
  nextU : Array Nat      -- nextU[i] = smallest k ≥ i with an unknown value (size when none)

namespace RangeAgg
def build (vals : Array R) : RangeAgg :=
  let n := vals.size
  let count (p : Tri → Bool) : Array Nat :=
    (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i => acc.push (acc[i]! + (if p vals[i]!.v then 1 else 0))) #[0]
  let nextU := (List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    acc.set! i (if vals[i]!.v = .u then i else acc[i + 1]!)) (Array.replicate (n + 1) n)
  ⟨vals, count (· = .f), count (· = .t), count (· = .u), nextU⟩

private def cnt (pref : Array Nat) (lo hi : Nat) : Nat := pref[hi + 1]! - pref[lo]!
private def firstUnknown (a : RangeAgg) (lo hi : Nat) : List UnknownReason :=
  let k := a.nextU[lo]!
  if k ≤ hi then a.vals[k]!.why else []

/-- ∧ over `lo … hi` inclusive; true on an empty range. -/
def all (a : RangeAgg) (lo hi : Nat) : R :=
  if hi < lo then R.t
  else if cnt a.prefF lo hi > 0 then R.f
  else if cnt a.prefU lo hi > 0 then ⟨.u, a.firstUnknown lo hi⟩
  else R.t
/-- ∨ over `lo … hi` inclusive; false on an empty range. -/
def any (a : RangeAgg) (lo hi : Nat) : R :=
  if hi < lo then R.f
  else if cnt a.prefT lo hi > 0 then R.t
  else if cnt a.prefU lo hi > 0 then ⟨.u, a.firstUnknown lo hi⟩
  else R.f

/-- The number of values among the first `m` that satisfy `p`: what `build` stores at `m`. -/
def countTo (vals : Array R) (p : Tri → Bool) : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | m + 1 => countTo vals p m + (if p vals[m]!.v then 1 else 0)

private theorem count_fold (vals : Array R) (p : Tri → Bool) (k : Nat) :
    ((List.range k).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i => acc.push (acc[i]! + (if p vals[i]!.v then 1 else 0))) #[0]).size = k + 1 ∧
    ∀ m, m ≤ k → ((List.range k).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
      acc.push (acc[i]! + (if p vals[i]!.v then 1 else 0))) #[0])[m]! = countTo vals p m := by
  induction k with
  | zero => simp [countTo]
  | succ k ih =>
    obtain ⟨hs, hv⟩ := ih
    simp only [List.range_succ, List.foldl_append, List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_nil]
    refine ⟨by simp [hs], fun m hm => ?_⟩
    rw [getElem!_pos _ m (by simp; omega), Array.getElem_push]
    split
    · rw [← getElem!_pos _ m (by omega)]; exact hv m (by omega)
    · obtain rfl : m = k + 1 := by omega
      simp only [countTo]; rw [hv k (Nat.le_refl _)]

theorem countTo_mono (vals : Array R) (p : Tri → Bool) {a b : Nat} (h : a ≤ b) :
    countTo vals p a ≤ countTo vals p b := by
  induction b with
  | zero => cases h; exact Nat.le_refl _
  | succ b ih =>
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge a (b + 1) with h' | h'
    · exact Nat.le_trans (ih (by omega)) (by simp only [countTo]; omega)
    · obtain rfl : a = b + 1 := by omega
      exact Nat.le_refl _

/-- The count rises between `lo` and `n` exactly when a value at an index in `[lo, n)` satisfies `p`. -/
theorem countTo_lt_iff (vals : Array R) (p : Tri → Bool) (lo n : Nat) :
    countTo vals p lo < countTo vals p n ↔ ∃ j, lo ≤ j ∧ j < n ∧ p vals[j]!.v := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    induction n with
    | zero => simp [countTo] at h
    | succ n ih =>
      by_cases hp : p vals[n]!.v
      · rcases Nat.lt_or_ge n lo with h' | h'
        · have := countTo_mono vals p (show n + 1 ≤ lo by omega); omega
        · exact ⟨n, h', Nat.lt_succ_self _, hp⟩
      · simp only [countTo, hp] at h
        obtain ⟨j, h1, h2, h3⟩ := ih (by simpa using h)
        exact ⟨j, h1, by omega, h3⟩
  · rintro ⟨j, h1, h2, h3⟩
    have a := countTo_mono vals p h1
    have b := countTo_mono vals p (show j + 1 ≤ n by omega)
    have c : countTo vals p (j + 1) = countTo vals p j + 1 := by simp [countTo, h3]
    omega

private theorem cnt_build_f (vals : Array R) (lo hi : Nat) (hl : lo ≤ hi) (h : hi < vals.size) :
    cnt (build vals).prefF lo hi = countTo vals (· = .f) (hi + 1) - countTo vals (· = .f) lo := by
  have hf := count_fold vals (· = .f) vals.size
  simp only [cnt, build]
  rw [hf.2 (hi + 1) (by omega), hf.2 lo (by omega)]

/-- `all` is false only on a definite false in the range. -/
theorem all_f_witness (vals : Array R) (lo hi : Nat) (h : ((build vals).all lo hi).v = .f) :
    ∃ j, lo ≤ j ∧ j ≤ hi ∧ j < vals.size ∧ vals[j]!.v = .f := by
  have hl : lo ≤ hi := by
    refine Nat.le_of_not_lt fun hn => ?_
    simp only [all, hn, if_true] at h
    exact absurd h (by decide)
  have hc : cnt (build vals).prefF lo hi > 0 := by
    refine Nat.pos_of_ne_zero fun hn => ?_
    simp only [all, show ¬ hi < lo by omega, if_false, hn, Nat.lt_irrefl] at h
    split at h <;> simp [R.t] at h
  have hhi : hi < vals.size := by
    refine Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hn => ?_
    have hf := count_fold vals (· = .f) vals.size
    have : (build vals).prefF[hi + 1]! = 0 := by
      simp only [build]; rw [getElem!_neg]; · rfl
      rw [hf.1]; omega
    simp only [cnt, this] at hc
    omega
  rw [cnt_build_f vals lo hi hl hhi] at hc
  obtain ⟨j, h1, h2, h3⟩ := (countTo_lt_iff vals (· = .f) lo (hi + 1)).1 (by omega)
  exact ⟨j, h1, by omega, by omega, by simpa using h3⟩

/-- A definite false in a range inside the array makes `all` false. -/
theorem all_f_of_witness (vals : Array R) (lo hi j : Nat) (hhi : hi < vals.size) (hlo : lo ≤ j) (hj : j ≤ hi)
    (hf : vals[j]!.v = .f) : (build vals).all lo hi = R.f := by
  have hc : cnt (build vals).prefF lo hi > 0 := by
    rw [cnt_build_f vals lo hi (by omega) hhi]
    have := (countTo_lt_iff vals (· = .f) lo (hi + 1)).2 ⟨j, hlo, by omega, by simp [hf]⟩
    omega
  simp only [all, show ¬ hi < lo by omega, if_false, hc, if_true]
end RangeAgg

end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Adequacy
3	  Mutation adequacy of a rule's witnesses: every leaf of the applicability and the obligation
4	  must do some work in some witness. A leaf is replaced by `tt` and by `ff` in turn; if neither
5	  replacement changes any scenario's episode verdict, the leaf is unexercised — the witnesses do
6	  not show that it matters, and a rule could carry an irrelevant atom without anyone noticing.
7	  Only the witnesses that expect a decided verdict count: a witness that expects unknown under a
8	  mask is decided by blanking any leaf that reads the masked atom, so it exercises nothing.
9	
10	  A concept call is one leaf: the rule's witnesses must show the concept matters, and the
11	  concept's own witnesses exercise its body.
12	
13	  Leaves of one atom that differ only in a literal argument (the values of one enumeration, each
14	  tested in its own disjunct) are one leaf in meaning: the family is unexercised only when none of
15	  its members moves a witness, and it is reported once.
16	
17	  Only the gate reads this file; rules never import it.
18	-/
19	import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
20	
21	namespace TrafficSpec
22	namespace Adequacy
23	
24	/-- The verdict tag one scenario produces for a rule: the episode verdict's tag, or the whole error. -/
25	def tagOf (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (cs : List Concept) (sc : Scenario) : String :=
26	  match sc.run ((rules.filter (·.id != r.id)) ++ [r]) cs with
27	  | .ok v => v.tag
28	  | .error e => s!"error:{e}"
29	
30	/-- The verdict tags a scenario list produces for a rule. -/
31	def profile (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (scs : List Scenario) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
32	  scs.map (tagOf rules r cs)
33	
34	/-- Whether the scenarios' tags for `r` differ from `base`, their tags for the unchanged rule
35	    (`profile rules r scs cs != base`), decided at the first scenario whose tag differs. -/
36	def moves (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (cs : List Concept) : List Scenario → List String → Bool
37	  | sc :: scs, b :: bs => if tagOf rules r cs sc != b then true else moves rules r cs scs bs
38	  | [], [] => false
39	  | _, _ => true
40	
41	/-- A leaf's family: its description with every literal argument blanked, so the leaves that
42	    test the values of one enumeration on the same atom and variables share a family. -/
43	def family (leaf : String) : String :=
44	  let marker := "Arg.lit \""
45	  match leaf.splitOn marker with
46	  | [] => leaf
47	  | first :: rest =>
48	    rest.foldl (fun acc piece =>
49	      let after := (piece.splitOn "\"").drop 1      -- drop the literal's text, keep what follows its closing quote
50	      acc ++ marker ++ "_\"" ++ "\"".intercalate after) first
51	
52	/-- One part's report, given its leaves (`names`, in order) and which of them move a witness: a
53	    family of literal variants counts once and only when no member moves, reported at its first
54	    leaf with the count of its members. A family's members are asked in order, and the first that
55	    moves settles it. -/
56	def report (label : String) (names : List String) (moved : Nat → Bool) : List String :=
57	  let fams := names.map family
58	  let firsts := (List.range names.length).filter fun k => !((fams.take k).contains (fams[k]?.getD ""))
59	  firsts.filterMap fun k =>
60	    let fam := fams[k]?.getD ""
61	    let members := (List.range names.length).filter fun j => fams[j]?.getD "" == fam
62	    if members.any moved then none
63	    else
64	      let note := if members.length > 1 then s!" (one of {members.length} literal variants of this atom; none exercised)" else ""
65	      some s!"{label} leaf {k}: {names[k]?.getD ""}{note}"
66	
67	/-- Leaves of the applicability and the obligation (binder classes are exercised by the
68	    grounding itself) that neither `tt` nor `ff` replacement moves any witness on, reported by
69	    `report`. -/
70	def unexercised (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (scs : List Scenario) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
71	  let decided := scs.filter fun sc => sc.expected.tag != "unknown"
72	  let base := profile rules r decided cs
73	  let check (label : String) (get : Rule → Formula) (put : Rule → Formula → Rule) : List String :=
74	    let φ := get r

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Adequacy
  Mutation adequacy of a rule's witnesses: every leaf of the applicability and the obligation
  must do some work in some witness. A leaf is replaced by `tt` and by `ff` in turn; if neither
  replacement changes any scenario's episode verdict, the leaf is unexercised — the witnesses do
  not show that it matters, and a rule could carry an irrelevant atom without anyone noticing.
  Only the witnesses that expect a decided verdict count: a witness that expects unknown under a
  mask is decided by blanking any leaf that reads the masked atom, so it exercises nothing.

  A concept call is one leaf: the rule's witnesses must show the concept matters, and the
  concept's own witnesses exercise its body.

  Leaves of one atom that differ only in a literal argument (the values of one enumeration, each
  tested in its own disjunct) are one leaf in meaning: the family is unexercised only when none of
  its members moves a witness, and it is reported once.

  Only the gate reads this file; rules never import it.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Adequacy

/-- The verdict tag one scenario produces for a rule: the episode verdict's tag, or the whole error. -/
def tagOf (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (cs : List Concept) (sc : Scenario) : String :=
  match sc.run ((rules.filter (·.id != r.id)) ++ [r]) cs with
  | .ok v => v.tag
  | .error e => s!"error:{e}"

/-- The verdict tags a scenario list produces for a rule. -/
def profile (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (scs : List Scenario) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
  scs.map (tagOf rules r cs)

/-- Whether the scenarios' tags for `r` differ from `base`, their tags for the unchanged rule
    (`profile rules r scs cs != base`), decided at the first scenario whose tag differs. -/
def moves (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (cs : List Concept) : List Scenario → List String → Bool
  | sc :: scs, b :: bs => if tagOf rules r cs sc != b then true else moves rules r cs scs bs
  | [], [] => false
  | _, _ => true

/-- A leaf's family: its description with every literal argument blanked, so the leaves that
    test the values of one enumeration on the same atom and variables share a family. -/
def family (leaf : String) : String :=
  let marker := "Arg.lit \""
  match leaf.splitOn marker with
  | [] => leaf
  | first :: rest =>
    rest.foldl (fun acc piece =>
      let after := (piece.splitOn "\"").drop 1      -- drop the literal's text, keep what follows its closing quote
      acc ++ marker ++ "_\"" ++ "\"".intercalate after) first

/-- One part's report, given its leaves (`names`, in order) and which of them move a witness: a
    family of literal variants counts once and only when no member moves, reported at its first
    leaf with the count of its members. A family's members are asked in order, and the first that
    moves settles it. -/
def report (label : String) (names : List String) (moved : Nat → Bool) : List String :=
  let fams := names.map family
  let firsts := (List.range names.length).filter fun k => !((fams.take k).contains (fams[k]?.getD ""))
  firsts.filterMap fun k =>
    let fam := fams[k]?.getD ""
    let members := (List.range names.length).filter fun j => fams[j]?.getD "" == fam
    if members.any moved then none
    else
      let note := if members.length > 1 then s!" (one of {members.length} literal variants of this atom; none exercised)" else ""
      some s!"{label} leaf {k}: {names[k]?.getD ""}{note}"

/-- Leaves of the applicability and the obligation (binder classes are exercised by the
    grounding itself) that neither `tt` nor `ff` replacement moves any witness on, reported by
    `report`. -/
def unexercised (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) (scs : List Scenario) (cs : List Concept := []) : List String :=
  let decided := scs.filter fun sc => sc.expected.tag != "unknown"
  let base := profile rules r decided cs
  let check (label : String) (get : Rule → Formula) (put : Rule → Formula → Rule) : List String :=
    let φ := get r
    report label (Formula.leaves φ) fun k => [Formula.tt, Formula.ff].any fun rep =>
      moves rules (put r (Formula.replaceLeaf k rep φ)) cs decided base
  check "applicability" (·.applicability) (fun r φ => { r with applicability := φ }) ++
  check "obligation" (·.obligation) (fun r φ => { r with obligation := φ })

end Adequacy
end TrafficSpec

    entranceOf := [marks], entranceObserved := true, marked := some true }

      (enters := some 10)
  , Build.lane 12 [(m (-4), m 6), (m 0, m 6), (m 0, m 40), (m (-4), m 40)] Build.south
      (enters := some 10)
  , Build.lane 13 [(m 6, m 0), (m 40, m 0), (m 40, m 4), (m 6, m 4)] Build.west
      (enters := some 10)
  , Build.lane 14 [(m (-40), m (-4)), (m (-6), m (-4)), (m (-6), m 0), (m (-40), m 0)] Build.east
      (enters := some 10)
  , crosswalk 20 (m (-6)) (m (-9)) (m 6) (m (-6)) 11
  , crosswalk 21 (m (-6)) (m 6) (m 6) (m 9) 12
  , crosswalk 22 (m 6) (m (-6)) (m 9) (m 6) 13
  , crosswalk 23 (m (-9)) (m (-6)) (m (-6)) (m 6) 14 ]

def motorbike : Q × Q × Q := (cm 110, cm 40, cm 70)

      junction

      , walker (mm (-11400 + 150 * (k : Int)), mm 7500) Build.east (m 3) ]
      junction
      [ signal [11] .left ]

    Build.scene t (some 1)
      [ rider 1 [.bicycle] pos hd (cm 480) yaw bike ]
      junction
      [ signal [11] .left ]

/-- `blind` (unknown): A motorcycle goes straight through on red with a green left arrow while a pedestrian on a crosswalk at the intersection is in predicted conflict with it; the source does not record which approach the crosswalk marks.

      junction

def branch_2Trace : Trace :=

# NRS_484B_307_9b_o4 — task result

## Final verdict

**OK** (gate run 1 of 6): 7 witnesses, 17 names, composes nothing.

## Gate runs

1. `OK`: the first and only run. Nothing was changed after it.

Before the gate run, one Bash call was mistaken. It was a compound no-op, meant as a placeholder,
that wrapped the gate command with `--help`. The permission layer denied it, so it did nothing.
An earlier `ls` of the Core directory went through; its output was used only to find the Core
file names.

## How the rule is written

- **Class of x (b2–b4):** five `ru_aggregate` atoms, one per claimed aggregate id, joined by `or`
  with `ru_motorcycle`.
- **Applicability (b1, b5, b6):** `existsRegion intersection i`, then one of three cases:
  - straight through (`drv_motion_straight_through_region`) under a red with either green arrow;
  - a right turn (`drv_motion_right_turn_through_region`) under `green_arrow(left)`;
  - a left turn (`drv_motion_left_turn_through_region`) under `green_arrow(right)`.

  Each movement is recognised at the exit. The signal is read at the entry with
  `since (¬ rises occupies(x,i)) (rises occupies(x,i) ∧ facing dir)`. `facing dir` means some
  `traffic_signal` s shows `circular_red` and `green_arrow(dir)`, and governs one of two things:
  - a `travel_region` c with `st_lane_enters(c, i)` that x occupied at the observation before the
    entry, or
  - i itself.

  The step bound is `p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph`. The upper end of both turn bands is
  `p.reversal_min_angle`.
- **Obligation (b12):** the rule selects i again with the applicability's whole selection
  (rule 3c). It then requires `¬ since (¬ rises occupies(x,i)) (¬ yieldsHere)`: no observation
  from the entry to the exit fails the duty. At one observation the duty applies where x occupies
  i and `drv_motion_moving` holds. For each pedestrian p (DEF-NRS-484A-165) and each member z of
  traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285, other than x), the duty is not both:
  - `prim_closest_approach_within` over `p.conflict_time_horizon`, and
  - `prim_closest_approach_distance < p.conflict_centre_clearance`.

  The pedestrians counted are those occupying a `crosswalk` w that `st_entrance_of` records as
  marking a `travel_region` c2 with `st_lane_enters(c2, i)`. The traffic counted is the members
  occupying i.

## Choices the node left open

- **"Occupied at the observation before the entry" (b5):** the language has no operator for the
  previous observation. This is written from one-step edges:
  `rises(¬occupies(x,c)) ∨ (occupies(x,c) ∧ ¬rises(occupies(x,c)))`, which is exactly
  "occupies(x,c) at the previous observation".
- **Each crossing judged once:** the duty is judged at the exit, over the observations since the
  last entry. The span is written as the record states it, so no narrowing is declared.
- **`¬ same(c2, i)` guard on the adjacent-crosswalk carrier:** an intersection is not a carrier
  that enters itself, so the guard leaves out nothing the record admits. Without it,
  `st_lane_enters(i, i)` is unknown, because an intersection carries no entry topology. That
  unknown would make the masked `blind` witness unknown for reasons other than `st.entrance_of`.
  The header explains this. It is not declared as a narrowing because it narrows nothing.
- **Narrowings:** none added. The record's own b2 and b12 narrowings are not restated.

## Witnesses

All seven use one four-arm junction with scenes 50 ms apart. Each names its instants from 50 ms
on, because the entry and exit edges are unknown at the first scene. The header of the witness
file describes the geometry.

| witness | verdict | scene |
|---|---|---|
| forbid | violated | bicycle straight through; pedestrian in the far crosswalk in predicted conflict |
| permit | compliant | bicycle stops in the intersection while the pedestrian crosses, then rides on |
| idle | not applicable | bicycle turns left with the left arrow |
| blind | unknown | `st.entrance_of` masked |
| branch_1 | compliant | motorcycle straight through, alone |
| branch_2 | violated | moped turns right in conflict with a car inside the intersection |
| branch_3 | violated | added: left turn under a green right arrow, with the signal governing the intersection itself |

- **permit** also exercises `drv_motion_moving`: the closest approach to the pedestrian while
  the bicycle stands would count as a conflict if it were moving.
- **branch_3** exercises the left-turn case and the `dev_governs(s, i)` case. The pedestrian is
  in the west crosswalk.

## Why I finished

The gate returned OK on the first run.

The rule and witnesses for NRS_484B_307_9b_o4 passed the gate with **OK** on the first run (7 witnesses, 17 names, 1 of 6 runs used). I wrote `task_result.md` in the working directory.

**The rule:**
- **Who it covers:** x is any of the five vehicle groups the law names (motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle, electric scooter), or anything labelled a motorcycle.
- **When it applies:** it is judged once per crossing, at the moment x leaves the intersection. It applies to:
  - going straight through under a red with either green arrow;
  - a right turn under a green left arrow;
  - a left turn under a green right arrow.

  The signal must have been showing red plus that arrow when x entered. It must have controlled either the lane x was in just before entering or the intersection itself.
- **The duty:** at every moment from entry to exit when x is in the intersection and moving, x must not be on course for a near-collision. That means coming closer than 4 m within the next 3 s, measured centre to centre. The duty covers pedestrians on a crosswalk at the intersection's approaches and any other road user in the intersection.

**Three choices the node left to me:**
- **"The lane just before entry":** the formula language has no way to say "at the previous moment", so I built it from start/stop edges of lane occupancy. It means exactly that.
- **An extra "not the intersection itself" check on the crosswalk's lane:** the data never says which lanes feed into the intersection area itself, so that test comes out undecided there. Without the check, the `blind` witness would be undecided for the wrong reason. The check excludes nothing the node allows, so I explained it in the file header and did not declare it as a narrowing.
- **No narrowings added.**

**Witnesses:** besides the six the node plans, I added `branch_3`, an electric bicycle turning left under a green right arrow, with the signal controlling the intersection itself. Without it, two parts of the formula (the left-turn case and the signal-controls-intersection case) would have no test.

**Mistaken shell call:** I ran one shell command other than the gate: a placeholder that wrapped the gate command with `--help`. It was blocked by the permissions and did nothing. An earlier `ls` of the Core folder did run and was used only to find file names.
